units.d: Saluer, se présenter, parler de soi
units.tip: « I have lived in Paris for two years » : pour une action qui dure encore, l'anglais utilise le present perfect + for, jamais le présent.
p: Je vais bien, merci. Et toi ?
I'm fine, thank you. And you?
I am fine, thanks. And you?
I am good, thank you. And you?
What do you do for a living?
J'habite à Paris depuis deux ans.
I have lived in Paris for two years.
I've been living in Paris for two years.
I have been living in Paris for two years.
I live near the city center.
I live near the city centre.
I like my job a lot.
I like my job very much.
c: be from = venir de : I am from…
L'âge se dit avec « be » : She is 25.
Avec you, le verbe be se conjugue are : How are you?
Pour l'origine, on dit be from : Where are you from?
À la 3e personne du singulier du présent, le verbe prend -s : she lives.
Devant un nom de métier, on met a ou an ; an devant un son voyelle : an engineer.
3e personne du singulier au présent : he works.

units.tip: Pour commander poliment : « I'd like… » ou « Could I have… ». « I want » sonne brusque.
p: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
I would like a coffee, please.
Could I have a coffee, please?
Can I have a coffee, please?
Could we have the check, please?
Could we have the bill, please?
Can we have the bill, please?
Do you have a table for two?
Je vais prendre la même chose.
I will have the same thing.
Un thé sans sucre, s'il vous plaît.
A tea with no sugar, please.
Je peux avoir un verre d'eau ?
Can I have a glass of water?
Could I have a glass of water?
May I have a glass of water?
Je voudrais réserver une table pour ce soir.
I'd like to book a table for tonight.
I would like to book a table for tonight.
I'd like to reserve a table for tonight.
c: Can I have the bill? = l'addition, s'il vous plaît.
Is service included? = le service est compris ?
an devant un son voyelle : an orange juice.
Can I have a glass ___ water?
Un contenant + of + contenu : a glass of water.
I'd like to ___ a table for two.
Réserver une table se dit book (ou reserve) a table.
Question au présent avec you : do + sujet + base verbale.
Le moyen de paiement : pay by card, mais pay in cash.

units.tip: « I have two brothers » ou « I've got two brothers » : les deux sont corrects (le second est plus britannique).
p: J'ai deux frères et une sœur.
I have two brothers and a sister.
I've got two brothers and a sister.
I have two brothers and one sister.
Mon meilleur ami habite à Londres.
My best friend lives in London.
We have dinner together on Sundays.
We eat dinner together on Sundays.
We have dinner together on Sunday.
Tu as des frères et sœurs ?
Do you have brothers and sisters?
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
Mon frère est plus grand que moi.
My brother is taller than me.
My brother is taller than I am.
Ma sœur a les cheveux longs.
Mes grands-parents sont à la retraite.
On se connaît depuis dix ans.
We have known each other for ten years.
We've known each other for ten years.
Je vois mes amis le samedi.
I see my friends on Saturdays.
I see my friends on Saturday.
c: L'âge s'exprime avec be : How old is he? He is 30.
Comparatif : older than (than = que). Then = ensuite.
___ you have any brothers or sisters?
Question au présent avec have : Do you have… ?
This is my friend Tom. ___ lives next door.
Sujet du verbe : he. His = son/sa, him = lui (complément).
Sujet pluriel (my parents) : have. Has va avec he / she / it.
Pour décrire les cheveux ou les yeux, on emploie have ; 3e personne : has.
Prendre un repas : have dinner. Avec we, pas de -s.
Devant un jour de la semaine, la préposition est on.

units.tip: Pour les habitudes : présent simple + adverbe de fréquence placé avant le verbe (I always get up early).
p: Je me lève à sept heures.
I get up at seven o'clock.
I wake up at seven o'clock.
Il est trois heures et demie.
Je prends le bus pour aller au travail.
I take the bus to work.
I go to work by bus.
I take the bus to go to work.
Le soir, je regarde des séries.
In the evening, I watch TV series.
In the evening, I watch series.
In the evening, I watch TV shows.
In the evening, I watch shows.
Je me couche tard le week-end.
I go to bed late on weekends.
I go to bed late at the weekend.
I go to bed late on the weekend.
Je suis toujours en retard le lundi.
I am always late on Mondays.
Il est neuf heures et quart.
It is a quarter past nine.
Le train part à six heures.
The train leaves at six o'clock.
Je prends une douche avant le petit-déjeuner.
I take a shower before breakfast.
I have a shower before breakfast.
Je commence le travail à neuf heures.
I start work at nine o'clock.
Je rentre à la maison vers dix-huit heures.
I get home around six p.m.
I get home at around six p.m.
I come home around six p.m.
Je prépare le dîner tous les soirs.
I read before going to sleep.
I read before I go to sleep.
c: Adverbe de fréquence avant le verbe principal.
She ___ to work by bus every day.
Habitude au présent simple, 3e personne : goes.
On + jour de la semaine ; in + mois ou année ; at + heure.
Question au présent simple avec you : do you finish… ?
I'm tired, so I'm going to bed ___ tonight.
Early = tôt. Quick est un adjectif, il ne convient pas ici.
Pour « et demie », on dit half past + heure.
Devant une heure précise (noon, midnight, 9 a.m.), la préposition est at.
Habitude au présent simple avec I : base verbale, have dinner.

units.tip: Pour dire ce qu'on aime : like / love / enjoy + -ing (I enjoy reading). Les adverbes de fréquence (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) se placent avant le verbe, mais après « be » (I'm always late).
p: I like reading in the evening.
I like to read in the evening.
I love reading in the evening.
I enjoy reading in the evening.
Je fais du sport deux fois par semaine.
I do sport twice a week.
I play sports twice a week.
I work out twice a week.
I do sports twice a week.
Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce week-end ?
What are you doing this weekend?
What are you doing at the weekend?
What are you up to this weekend?
I often go to the cinema.
I often go to the movies.
Je ne regarde jamais la télé.
Shall we go hiking on Sunday?
Do you want to go hiking on Sunday?
Should we go hiking on Sunday?
Mon passe-temps préféré, c'est la cuisine.
Il joue au foot une fois par semaine.
He plays soccer once a week.
He plays football once a week.
Ça te dit d'aller au cinéma ?
Would you like to go to the movies?
Would you like to go to the cinema?
Do you want to go to the movies?
Do you want to go to the cinema?
Désolé, je ne peux pas samedi.
I'm sorry, I can't on Saturday.
Sorry, I can't make it on Saturday.
On se retrouve à quelle heure ?
c: L'adverbe de fréquence se place avant le verbe.
Avec « be », l'adverbe se place après le verbe : I'm always tired.
Après like, love, enjoy, hate : verbe en -ing.
3e personne du singulier au présent : she loves.
Shall we + base verbale sert à proposer une activité.
Would you like ___ to the movies?
Après would like, on met to + base verbale.
Projet proche : présent en be + -ing, What are you doing?

units.tip: Dénombrable ou non ? « some apples » mais « some bread » ; « How many eggs? » mais « How much milk? ». Pour une recette, on utilise l'impératif : « Chop the onions, add the salt ».
p: Il nous faut du pain et des œufs.
We need some bread and some eggs.
We need some bread and eggs.
How many apples do you want?
How many apples would you like?
How much does the cheese cost?
Coupe les oignons en petits morceaux.
Cut the onions into small pieces.
Chop the onions into small pieces.
Il n'y a plus de lait.
Un kilo de tomates, s'il vous plaît.
Il reste un peu de fromage.
There is a little cheese left.
Il n'y a pas assez d'œufs.
Mélange le beurre et le sucre.
Mix the butter and the sugar.
c: run out of = ne plus avoir de.
eggs est au pluriel : Where are…?
milk est indénombrable : much (many pour ce qui se compte).
Une durée s'exprime avec for : for twenty minutes.
Couper en morceaux : cut into pieces.
Une consigne de recette est à l'impératif : la base verbale seule.

units.tip: « Can I try it on? » : on/off/up sont des particules qui changent le sens du verbe (phrasal verbs).
p: Excusez-moi, où est la gare la plus proche ?
Excuse me, where is the nearest train station?
Excuse me, where's the nearest train station?
Excuse me, where is the closest train station?
Tournez à gauche au deuxième feu.
Turn left at the second traffic light.
Turn left at the second light.
C'est à dix minutes à pied.
It is ten minutes on foot.
Do you have it in a larger size?
Do you have it in a bigger size?
Do you have this in a bigger size?
Do you have this in a larger size?
I am just looking, thank you.
Le train a été annulé à cause de la grève.
The train was canceled because of the strike.
The train was cancelled because of the strike.
The train has been canceled because of the strike.
The train has been cancelled because of the strike.
Go straight ahead to the bridge.
Go straight on to the bridge.
Un aller-retour pour Londres, s'il vous plaît.
A return ticket to London, please.
A round-trip ticket to London, please.
A round trip to London, please.
De quel quai part le train ?
Which platform does the train leave from?
What platform does the train leave from?
Le prochain bus passe dans dix minutes.
The next bus comes in ten minutes.
The next bus is in ten minutes.
The next bus comes in 10 minutes.
c: go straight ahead = continuer tout droit.
How much is it? = combien ça coûte ?
The station is ___ the bank and the post office.
between A and B = entre deux éléments.
Pour un point précis du trajet, on dit at : at the traffic lights.
Horaire fixe : présent simple ; 3e personne → leaves.
Which platform does the train leave ___?
Do you have this shirt in a ___ size?

parts.t: Prends le train et le bus

units.d: Chez le médecin, à la pharmacie
units.tip: Les douleurs : headache, stomachache, backache… On dit « I have a headache » (avec a).
p: Je dois prendre rendez-vous chez le médecin.
I need to make an appointment with the doctor.
I have to make an appointment with the doctor.
I need to book an appointment with the doctor.
Depuis combien de temps avez-vous de la fièvre ?
How long have you had a fever?
How long have you had a temperature?
Je me sens beaucoup mieux aujourd'hui.
I am feeling much better today.
Je fais du sport trois fois par semaine.
I work out three times a week.
I exercise three times a week.
I do sport three times a week.
Où est la pharmacie la plus proche ?
I've been coughing for three days.
I have been coughing for three days.
Prenez un comprimé après chaque repas.
Take one tablet after each meal.
Take a tablet after each meal.
Take one pill after each meal.
Take a pill after each meal.
Je dors huit heures par nuit.
I sleep eight hours a night.
I sleep for eight hours a night.
c: How long ___ you had this cough?
Durée jusqu'à maintenant : present perfect (have had).
You ___ see a doctor about that.
Fréquence : twice a day, once a week.
Mal de tête = headache (de même : stomachache, toothache).
Since + point de départ (Monday) ; for + durée (for three days).
You'll feel better if you ___ some rest.
Après if (condition réelle), le présent : if you get… you'll feel…
water est indénombrable : more water (et non many).
Pour une habitude : every + nom singulier (every morning).

units.tip: Américain : apartment, landlord ; britannique : flat. Les deux sont compris partout.
p: Je cherche un appartement de deux pièces.
I'm looking for a two-room apartment.
I am looking for a two-room apartment.
I'm looking for a one-bedroom apartment.
I'm looking for a two-room flat.
Le loyer est de mille euros par mois.
The rent is a thousand euros a month.
The rent is one thousand euros a month.
The rent is a thousand euros per month.
The rent is 1,000 euros a month.
The heating is not working anymore.
Mes voisins font beaucoup de bruit.
My neighbors make a lot of noise.
My neighbours make a lot of noise.
Quand est-ce que je peux emménager ?
Il faut signer le bail avant vendredi.
The lease must be signed before Friday.
You need to sign the lease before Friday.
We need to sign the lease before Friday.
Le propriétaire va réparer la fuite.
The landlord is going to fix the leak.
The landlord will fix the leak.
The landlord is going to repair the leak.
Il y a une fuite dans la salle de bains.
There's a leak in the bathroom.
There is a leak in the bathroom.
La machine à laver est en panne.
I've just moved in next door.
I just moved in next door.
I have just moved in next door.
Could you turn the music down?
Could you turn down the music?
Can you turn the music down?
Can you turn down the music?
Ma voisine arrose mes plantes quand je pars.
My neighbor waters my plants when I'm away.
My neighbour waters my plants when I'm away.
My neighbor waters my plants when I am away.
On se dit bonjour dans l'escalier.
We say hello on the stairs.
We say hi on the stairs.
c: I'm looking ___ a flat near the center.
Emménager : move in ; déménager : move out.
The sink is ___. Can you fix it?
Une action en cours : be + -ing (is leaking).
I'll ___ the landlord about the heating.
Appeler quelqu'un : call + personne, sans préposition.
Could you turn the music ___, please?
Baisser le son : turn down ; l'éteindre : turn off.

units.tip: « I've never been to Japan » : been to = expérience de voyage. « He has gone to Japan » = il y est (encore) parti.
p: J'ai réservé un hôtel près de la plage.
I booked a hotel near the beach.
I've booked a hotel near the beach.
I have booked a hotel near the beach.
Est-ce que le petit-déjeuner est inclus ?
Nous sommes partis une semaine en Italie.
We went to Italy for a week.
We spent a week in Italy.
I have never taken a plane.
Could you take a picture of us?
Could you take a photo of us?
Il y a un vol direct pour Tokyo ?
Is there a direct flight to Tokyo?
Je voudrais un siège côté hublot.
I would like a window seat.
J'ai une réservation au nom de Martin.
I have a reservation under the name Martin.
I have a booking under the name Martin.
I have a reservation in the name of Martin.
La chambre donne sur la mer.
The room has a sea view.
À quelle heure faut-il libérer la chambre ?
What time do we have to check out?
What time do I have to check out?
Il a fait beau toute la semaine.
The weather was nice all week.
The weather was good all week.
On a goûté la cuisine locale.
c: What time does the flight ___ off?
Could I have a room ___ a sea view?
A room with a view / with a balcony.
I'd like to check ___, please. Here is my key.
Check in = arriver à l'hôtel ; check out = rendre la chambre.
We're looking forward to ___ the old town.
Look forward to + -ing : to est ici une préposition.
Your flight ___ delayed by an hour.
Passif au present perfect : has been + participe passé.
Could I have an ___ seat, please?
Une place côté couloir se dit an aisle seat (le s ne se prononce pas).

units.d: Se présenter au téléphone, patienter, rappeler, fixer un rendez-vous
units.tip: Au téléphone : « This is Léa » (et non « I am Léa »), « Could I speak to… ? », « Hold on, please », « I'll call you back ». Pour fixer un rendez-vous : « Does Tuesday work for you? ».
p: Could I speak to Mr. Smith?
May I speak to Mr. Smith?
Could I speak with Mr. Smith?
Can I speak to Mr. Smith?
Ne quittez pas, s'il vous plaît.
Je vous rappelle dans cinq minutes.
I'll call you back in five minutes.
I will call you back in five minutes.
I'll call you back in 5 minutes.
I'd like to make an appointment.
I would like to make an appointment.
I'd like to book an appointment.
Désolé, je me suis trompé de numéro.
Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
Sorry, I've got the wrong number.
Sorry, I have the wrong number.
I can't hear you very well.
Il n'est pas là pour le moment.
He's not here at the moment.
He isn't here at the moment.
He is not here at the moment.
He's not in at the moment.
Pouvez-vous lui dire de me rappeler ?
Can you tell him to call me back?
Could you tell him to call me back?
Could you ask him to call me back?
Can you ask him to call me back?
I need to cancel my appointment.
I have to cancel my appointment.
On peut le reporter à jeudi ?
Can we move it to Thursday?
Could we move it to Thursday?
Can we postpone it to Thursday?
Can we postpone it until Thursday?
c: Does it work for you? = ça te convient ?
Prendre un message : take a message.
Être en réunion : be in a meeting.
Can we ___ the meeting to Monday?
Déplacer un rendez-vous : move it to + jour (ou reschedule).
Devant un jour, même suivi de afternoon, la préposition est on.

units.d: Would you like…, How about…, refuser poliment
units.tip: Pour inviter : « Would you like to… ? », « How about… ? ». Pour refuser poliment, donne une raison et propose autre chose : « I'd love to, but I'm busy. Maybe next week? ».
p: Ça te dirait de venir dîner samedi ?
Would you like to come for dinner on Saturday?
Would you like to come to dinner on Saturday?
Do you want to come for dinner on Saturday?
J'aimerais bien, mais je suis pris.
I'd love to, but I'm busy.
I'd like to, but I'm busy.
I'd love to, but I'm not free.
Et si on allait au cinéma ?
How about going to the cinema?
How about going to the movies?
What about going to the movies?
Why don't we go to the cinema?
Why don't we go to the movies?
Est-ce que je peux venir avec un ami ?
Can I come with a friend?
Are you free on Friday evening?
Are you free on Friday night?
J'organise une fête pour mon anniversaire.
I'm having a party for my birthday.
I'm throwing a party for my birthday.
I'm organizing a party for my birthday.
Désolé, j'ai déjà quelque chose de prévu.
I'm sorry, I already have plans.
Ce n'est pas possible pour moi cette semaine.
I can't make it this week.
This week doesn't work for me.
It's not possible for me this week.
c: I'd love to, ___ I'm working that day.
On reprend l'infinitif sans le verbe : I'd love to.
Sorry, I can't ___ it on Saturday.

units.d: Batterie, wifi, mots de passe, applications qui plantent
units.tip: Pour décrire un souci technique : « It doesn't work », « It keeps crashing », « The battery is dead ». Verbes utiles : charge, download, update, log in (verbe en deux mots) / login (nom).
p: Mon téléphone n'a plus de batterie.
My phone has run out of battery.
Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?
Je dois mettre à jour mon ordinateur.
I need to update my computer.
I have to update my computer.
Je n'arrive pas à me connecter.
Can you send me the link?
Could you send me the link?
J'ai oublié mon mot de passe.
Est-ce que tu as un chargeur ?
Je t'envoie les photos par e-mail.
I'll send you the photos by email.
I'm sending you the photos by email.
I'll send you the pictures by email.
Can you add me to the group?
c: I can't log ___ to my account.
My phone has run out ___ battery.
run out of = ne plus avoir de.
Could you send me the ___ to the video?
Devant un nom : adjectif possessif my (mine s'emploie seul).
Turn the router off and ___ again.
Allumer : turn on ; éteindre : turn off.
Can you send me the file ___ email?
Le moyen d'envoi : by email, by post.

units.d: will, going to, présent progressif, when + présent
units.tip: « Going to » pour une intention déjà décidée (I'm going to move), « will » pour une décision prise sur le moment ou une prédiction (I'll help you), présent progressif pour un rendez-vous fixé (I'm meeting Sam tomorrow). Après « when / as soon as », jamais de « will ».
p: I'm going to move next year.
I am going to move next year.
I am seeing Sam tomorrow evening.
Il va pleuvoir, regarde les nuages.
It's going to rain, look at the clouds.
It is going to rain, look at the clouds.
Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire après tes études ?
What are you going to do after your studies?
What are you going to do after you graduate?
What will you do after your studies?
Le train part à huit heures.
The train leaves at eight o'clock.
As soon as I arrive, I'll call you.
As soon as I arrive, I will call you.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.
I'm going to learn to drive.
I am going to learn to drive.
I'm going to learn how to drive.
We're going to buy a house.
We are going to buy a house.
Je pense qu'il fera beau demain.
I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
I think the weather will be nice tomorrow.
I think it'll be sunny tomorrow.
I'm going on vacation on Saturday.
I'm going on holiday on Saturday.
I'm leaving on vacation on Saturday.
Le film commence à vingt heures.
The movie starts at eight p.m.
The film starts at eight p.m.
Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce soir ?
What are you doing this evening?
c: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
Prédiction fondée sur un indice visible : going to.
When I ___ home, I'll call you.
Après when / as soon as : présent (pas de will).
— The phone is ringing. — I ___ answer it!
Décision prise sur le moment : will.
I ___ my dentist at 3 p.m. tomorrow.
We're ___ to buy a new car.
Projet décidé : be going to + base verbale.
Dans be going to, l'auxiliaire est be : are you…?
Rendez-vous déjà fixé : présent en be + -ing.

units.tip: « look forward to » est suivi de -ing : I'm looking forward to seeing you.
p: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait ce week-end ?
What did you do this weekend?
What did you do over the weekend?
What did you do at the weekend?
Je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord avec toi.
I don't quite agree with you.
I don't completely agree with you.
I don't fully agree with you.
I don't totally agree with you.
I do not quite agree with you.
J'ai hâte de partir en vacances.
I'm looking forward to going on vacation.
I can't wait to go on vacation.
I'm looking forward to going on holiday.
I can't wait to go on holiday.
I am looking forward to going on vacation.
If I were you, I would call him.
If I were you, I'd call him.
If I were you, I would call her.
If I were you, I'd call her.
Je me suis mis au yoga récemment.

I would like to learn to play the guitar.
J'ai hâte de voir le film.

I can't wait to see the film.

I'm looking forward to seeing the film.
Je me suis mise à la course à pied.
c: « look forward to » : to est une préposition → verbe en -ing.
If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
Conditionnel irréel : If I were you (were pour toutes les personnes).
since + point de départ ; for + durée.
How have you been? : present perfect, pour « depuis la dernière fois ».
Be up to something : faire quelque chose, s'occuper.

units.tip: Prétérit = action terminée ; past continuous = action en cours ; past perfect = action antérieure à une autre action passée.
p: Pendant que je cuisinais, le téléphone a sonné.
While I was cooking, the phone rang.
Quand je suis arrivé, tout le monde était déjà parti.
When I arrived, everyone had already left.
When I got there, everyone had already left.
We've known each other since childhood.
We have known each other since childhood.
We've known each other since we were kids.
Je ne l'avais jamais vu aussi heureux.
I had never seen him so happy.
I'd never seen him so happy.
I had never seen him this happy.
I used to live in the countryside.
I used to live in the country.
Tout à coup, il s'est mis à pleuvoir.
All of a sudden, it started to rain.
In the end, everything turned out fine.
In the end, everything worked out.
In the end, it all worked out.
Tu ne devineras jamais ce qui s'est passé !

Il faisait nuit et il pleuvait.
It was dark and it was raining.
It was night and it was raining.
Tout à coup, la lumière s'est éteinte.
All of a sudden, the lights went out.
Ensuite, nous avons appelé la police.
After that, we called the police.
In the end, we had a good laugh.
In the end, we laughed a lot.

Je m'en souviendrai toute ma vie.
I'll remember it all my life.
I will remember it all my life.
I'll remember it for the rest of my life.
c: I ___ in Lyon when I was a child.
Habitude passée : used to + base verbale.
While she ___ TV, the lights went out.
Action en cours interrompue : past continuous.
By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.
Antériorité dans le passé : past perfect.
I ___ my keys, so I couldn't get in.
Action antérieure à une autre action passée : past perfect (had + participe passé).
Événement ponctuel dans un récit : prétérit.
In the ___, we found the hotel.
Finalement, au bout du compte : in the end.
We laughed ___ much that we cried.
so + adverbe ou adjectif + that : tellement… que.

units.tip: Pour nuancer sans heurter : « I see what you mean, but… », « That's a fair point, however… ».
p: À mon avis, c'est une perte de temps.

In my opinion, it is a waste of time.

Je vois ce que tu veux dire, mais…

agree with someone ; agree on something.
I see your point, ___ I still disagree.
On concède puis on s'oppose : I see your point, but…
To some extent = dans une certaine mesure : pour nuancer son accord.
On the one hand it's cheap; on the ___ hand, it's slow.
On the one hand… on the other hand… = d'un côté… de l'autre…
I'm not ___ that it will work.
Faire chacun un pas vers l'autre : meet halfway.

units.d: ever, never, already, yet, just, for/since
units.tip: Present perfect = lien avec le présent, sans date précise (I've been to Japan). Dès qu'il y a une date ou un moment passé (yesterday, in 2019, last year), on passe au prétérit (I went to Japan in 2019). For = durée, since = point de départ.
p: Je suis déjà allé au Japon.
I have already been to Japan.
Tu as déjà mangé des sushis ?
Je n'ai jamais vu la neige.
I have been living here since 2018.
Je la connais depuis dix ans.
I've known her for ten years.
I have known her for ten years.
Je suis allé à Rome l'été dernier.
I went to Rome last summer.
Tu es déjà monté à cheval ?
Have you ever ridden a horse?
Have you ever been horse riding?
J'ai déjà vu ce film deux fois.
I've already seen this movie twice.
I have already seen this movie twice.
I've already seen this film twice.
I have already seen this film twice.
I've been learning English for six months.
I have been learning English for six months.
Ça fait longtemps que tu travailles ici ?
Have you been working here long?
Have you been working here for a long time?
Have you worked here for a long time?
I have known her since school.
c: Expérience sans date : present perfect (have been = y être allé et revenu).
yet en fin de question : déjà ?
Dans une question sur l'expérience : ever (déjà, un jour).
I've never ___ such a beautiful place.
She ___ the email an hour ago.
Avec ago (moment passé précis), on emploie le prétérit.

parts.t: Situe un fait dans le passé

units.tip: Vocabulaire utile : open an account, withdraw cash, a fee (des frais), fill in / fill out a form, an ID. « I'd like to… » reste la formule passe-partout pour demander un service.

Could you fill in this form?

an devant un son voyelle : an account.
Payer en espèces : pay in cash (mais pay by card).

units.tip: En urgence : « Call an ambulance! », « I've lost my wallet », « Someone stole my phone ». On compose le 999 au Royaume-Uni, le 911 aux États-Unis et le 112 partout en Europe.
p: Ma voiture est tombée en panne.
Où est le commissariat le plus proche ?

Pour une partie du corps, l'anglais emploie le possessif : his arm.
Un pneu crevé : a flat tire (flat tyre en anglais britannique).

parts.t: Signale une perte ou un vol

units.d: aren't you?, does she?, shall we?, Do you know what time it is?, Who called you? / Who did you call?, He told me he was…
units.tip: Le question tag reprend l'auxiliaire en inversant le signe : You're coming, aren't you? / She doesn't eat meat, does she? Question sur le sujet : pas d'auxiliaire (Who called you?) ; sur le complément : did (Who did you call?). Au discours rapporté, les temps reculent : « I'm tired » → he said he was tired.
p: Tu viens ce soir, n'est-ce pas ?
You are coming tonight, aren't you?
Do you know what time it is?
Il m'a dit qu'il était fatigué.
He told me he was tired.
He told me that he was tired.
He said that he was tired.
She asked me where I lived.
Who did you call last night?
Je ne sais pas s'il viendra.
I don't know if he'll come.
I don't know whether he'll come.
I don't know if he will come.
I don't know whether he will come.
I don't know if he's coming.
I don't know whether he's coming.

Do you know where the train station is?

Elle m'a demandé si j'avais faim.
She asked me if I was hungry.

Ils ont dit qu'ils étaient en retard.
They said that they were late.
c: Phrase affirmative avec be → tag négatif avec be : aren't you?
Phrase négative → tag affirmatif avec le même auxiliaire : does she?
Après Let's, le tag est toujours shall we?
Question indirecte : sujet + verbe (what time it is).
Discours rapporté au passé : is → was.
Question rapportée : pas d'auxiliaire did, temps reculé.
Who est sujet : pas d'auxiliaire (Who gave you…?).
Who est complément : auxiliaire did (Who did you call?).
I don't know ___ he'll come or not.
whether… or not = si… ou non.

units.tip: Regret au passé : should have + participe passé (I should have left earlier).
p: Je suis débordé en ce moment.
I am swamped at the moment.
I'm snowed under at the moment.
Ne t'en fais pas, ce n'est pas grave.
Don't worry, it's no big deal.
Don't worry, it's not a big deal.
Don't worry about it, it's no big deal.
Mon vol a été retardé de trois heures.
My flight was delayed by three hours.
My flight has been delayed by three hours.
My flight was delayed three hours.
Ça m'est sorti de la tête.
On est dans le même bateau.

Je ne m'y attendais pas du tout.

I did not expect that at all.
Je n'ai pas une minute à moi.

It's not the end of the world.
It isn't the end of the world.

Je n'aurais pas dû dire ça.
I should not have said that.

Irréel du passé : If + had + participe passé, would have + participe passé.
You ___ have told me earlier! I was waiting for hours.
Reproche sur le passé : should have + participe passé.
I'm not used to ___ up so early.
be used to + -ing = être habitué à.
I'm so busy I can't keep ___ with my emails.
Suivre le rythme : keep up with.

work est indénombrable : too much work (trop de travail).
Ce n'est pas grave : it's no big deal (expression figée).
Regret sur le passé : I wish + past perfect.

units.tip: Un phrasal verb change de sens avec sa particule : give up (abandonner), give in (céder), give back (rendre).
p: Il faut que je règle ce problème.

units.d: if + présent / prétérit / past perfect, I wish, unless, in case
units.tip: If + présent → will (réel) ; if + prétérit → would (hypothèse : If I had time, I would travel) ; if + past perfect → would have + participe (regret : If I had known, I would have come). Jamais de « would » après « if ».
p: Si j'avais plus de temps, je voyagerais.
If I had more time, I would travel.
If I had more time, I'd travel.
Si j'avais su, je serais venu.
If I had known, I would have come.
If I'd known, I would have come.
If I had known, I'd have come.
If I'd known, I'd have come.
S'il pleut, nous resterons à la maison.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it rains, we'll stay home.
If it rains, we'll stay at home.
If it rains, we will stay home.
If I were you, I would accept.
If I were you, I'd accept.
If I were you, I'd accept it.
Que ferais-tu si tu gagnais au loto ?
What would you do if you won the lottery?
Sauf s'il y a des bouchons, je serai à l'heure.
Unless there's traffic, I'll be on time.
Unless there is traffic, I will be on time.
I'll be on time unless there's traffic.
Si tu chauffes la glace, elle fond.
If you heat ice, it melts.

What would you do in my place?

Regret sur le passé : would have + participe.

wish + prétérit : I wish I could.

Hypothèse sur le présent : if + prétérit, puis would.

Regret sur le passé : would have + participe passé.
